//! Helpers shared by the WAV-based integration tests.

#![allow(dead_code)]

use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use nalgebra::DMatrix;

pub const DATA_DIR: &str = "./tests/data/single-source";

/// Ground truth encoded in a test-data filename.
pub struct Meta {
    pub frequency_hz: f64,
    pub doa_deg: f64,
    pub duration_s: f64,
}

/// Parse `single-source_<freq>Hz_<doa>deg_<duration>s.wav`.
pub fn parse_meta(path: &Path) -> Meta {
    let stem = path
        .file_stem()
        .and_then(|s| s.to_str())
        .expect("bad file name");
    let parts: Vec<&str> = stem.split('_').collect();
    let num = |s: &str, suffix: &str| -> f64 { s.strip_suffix(suffix).unwrap().parse().unwrap() };
    Meta {
        frequency_hz: num(parts[1], "Hz"),
        doa_deg: num(parts[2], "deg"),
        duration_s: num(parts[3], "s"),
    }
}

/// All WAV files in the single-source data directory, sorted by name.
pub fn wav_files() -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let mut paths: Vec<PathBuf> = fs::read_dir(DATA_DIR)
        .expect("Test data directory not found")
        .map(|e| e.unwrap().path())
        .filter(|p| p.extension().and_then(|ext| ext.to_str()) == Some("wav"))
        .collect();
    paths.sort();
    paths
}

/// Read a 4-channel, 24-bit PCM WAV file with `hound` and return
/// `(sample_rate, data)` where `data` is a `(4 × n_samples)` real matrix
/// normalised to `[-1, 1]`.
pub fn read_wav_4ch(path: &Path) -> (u32, DMatrix<f64>) {
    let mut reader = hound::WavReader::open(path).expect("Failed to open WAV file");
    let spec = reader.spec();
    assert_eq!(spec.channels, 4, "Expected 4-channel WAV");
    assert_eq!(spec.bits_per_sample, 24, "Expected 24-bit PCM");

    let raw_samples: Vec<i32> = reader
        .samples::<i32>()
        .map(|s| s.expect("Sample read error"))
        .collect();

    let n_channels = spec.channels as usize;
    let n_samples = raw_samples.len() / n_channels;
    let scale = 2.0_f64.powi(23); // 24-bit signed → [-1, 1]

    // De-interleave: WAV stores [ch0, ch1, ch2, ch3, ch0, ch1, ...]
    let mut data = DMatrix::<f64>::zeros(n_channels, n_samples);
    for (idx, &sample) in raw_samples.iter().enumerate() {
        data[(idx % n_channels, idx / n_channels)] = sample as f64 / scale;
    }

    (spec.sample_rate, data)
}

/// Smallest circular distance in degrees between `estimate_deg` and any of `truths_deg`.
pub fn angular_error(estimate_deg: f64, truths_deg: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    truths_deg
        .iter()
        .map(|&t| {
            let d = (estimate_deg - t).rem_euclid(360.0);
            d.min(360.0 - d)
        })
        .fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min)
}

// Integration tests for musicrs
//
// Tests DOA estimation against the pre-recorded single-source WAV test data.
// Each WAV file is a 4-channel, 24-bit PCM, 16 kHz recording whose filename
// encodes the source frequency, true DOA, and duration.

mod common;

use musicrs::MusicEstimator;

/// For every WAV file in `tests/data/single-source/`, estimate the DOA of the
/// single source and verify it is within ±5° of the ground-truth angle encoded
/// in the filename.
#[test]
#[ignore = "slow"]
fn test_single_source_doa() {
    let estimator = MusicEstimator::default();
    let tolerance_deg = 5.0_f64;

    let mut total = 0usize;
    let mut failures: Vec<String> = Vec::new();

    for path in common::wav_files() {
        let meta = common::parse_meta(&path);
        let name = path.file_name().unwrap().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        let (sample_rate, real_data) = common::read_wav_4ch(&path);
        assert_eq!(sample_rate as f64, estimator.sample_rate);
        total += 1;

        let estimated_angles = estimator.estimate_doa_from_real(&real_data, 1, meta.frequency_hz);
        let Some(estimate) = estimated_angles.first() else {
            failures.push(format!(
                "{name}: no peak found (expected {:.1}°)",
                meta.doa_deg
            ));
            continue;
        };
        let estimated_deg = estimate.to_degrees();

        // A linear x-axis array has mirror symmetry: a(θ) = a(360°−θ).
        // At exactly Nyquist (f == sr/2), the real steering vector adds two more
        // equivalent angles: a(θ) = a(180°−θ) = a(180°+θ).
        let nyquist = sample_rate as f64 / 2.0;
        let truth = meta.doa_deg;
        let equivalent_angles: Vec<f64> = if (meta.frequency_hz - nyquist).abs() < 0.5 {
            vec![truth, 360.0 - truth, 180.0 - truth, 180.0 + truth]
        } else {
            vec![truth, 360.0 - truth]
        };
        let error = common::angular_error(estimated_deg, &equivalent_angles);

        if error > tolerance_deg {
            failures.push(format!(
                "{name}: expected {truth:.1}° (equivalents: {equivalent_angles:?}), got {estimated_deg:.1}° (error {error:.1}°)"
            ));
        }
    }

    if !failures.is_empty() {
        panic!(
            "{}/{} files failed DOA accuracy test (tolerance ±{:.0}°):\n{}",
            failures.len(),
            total,
            tolerance_deg,
            failures.join("\n")
        );
    }

    println!("All {total} single-source DOA tests passed (tolerance ±{tolerance_deg:.0}°).");
}

// IFB-MUSIC on the single-source WAV data, using the one STFT bin that holds the tone.
//
// nfft = 160 at 16 kHz gives 100 Hz bins, so every test tone falls exactly on a bin.
// Tones at or above Nyquist are excluded: at Nyquist the DOA is ambiguous
// (θ, 180° ± θ), and above it the STFT only sees the aliased frequency.

mod common;

use musicrs::MusicEstimator;

const NFFT: usize = 160;

#[test]
fn ifb_single_bin_doa() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    let tolerance_deg = 5.0_f64;
    let nyquist = est.sample_rate / 2.0;

    let mut total = 0usize;
    let mut failures = Vec::new();

    for path in common::wav_files() {
        let meta = common::parse_meta(&path);
        if meta.frequency_hz >= nyquist {
            continue;
        }
        let (sample_rate, data) = common::read_wav_4ch(&path);
        assert_eq!(sample_rate as f64, est.sample_rate);
        let bin = (meta.frequency_hz * NFFT as f64 / est.sample_rate).round() as usize;

        let (spectrum, angles) = est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&[bin]));
        let argmax = (0..spectrum.len())
            .max_by(|&a, &b| spectrum[a].total_cmp(&spectrum[b]))
            .unwrap();
        let estimated_deg = angles[argmax].to_degrees();
        let error = common::angular_error(estimated_deg, &[meta.doa_deg, 360.0 - meta.doa_deg]);
        total += 1;
        if error > tolerance_deg {
            failures.push(format!(
                "{}: expected {:.1}°, got {estimated_deg:.1}° (error {error:.1}°)",
                path.file_name().unwrap().to_string_lossy(),
                meta.doa_deg
            ));
        }
    }

    assert!(total > 0, "no test files below Nyquist");
    assert!(
        failures.is_empty(),
        "{}/{total} files failed IFB DOA test (tolerance ±{tolerance_deg:.0}°):\n{}",
        failures.len(),
        failures.join("\n")
    );
    println!("All {total} IFB single-bin DOA tests passed (tolerance ±{tolerance_deg:.0}°).");
}

// Parity with the original pyMUSIC implementation.
//
// The CSVs in tests/golden/ were produced by running pyMUSIC on the WAV test data
// (see tests/golden/generate_golden.py), in two variants:
//   * `*.eigh.csv` – pyMUSIC with `np.linalg.eig` swapped for the Hermitian `eigh`.
//     musicrs must match these value-by-value.
//   * `*.eig.csv`  – pyMUSIC as published. On this nearly noiseless data `eig`
//     returns a non-orthogonal noise basis, so the values are basis-dependent; only
//     the peak location is compared.

mod common;

use std::fs;
use std::path::Path;

use musicrs::{MusicEstimator, analytic_signal};
use nalgebra::DMatrix;

const GOLDEN_DIR: &str = "./tests/golden";
const NFFT: usize = 160;
// Noise eigenvalues are ~1e-15 and pyMUSIC builds steering vectors in float128,
// so agreement is ~1e-7..1e-6 rather than machine precision.
const REL_TOLERANCE: f64 = 1e-4;

const CASES: [(&str, f64); 3] = [
    ("single-source_300Hz_80deg_1.0s", 300.0),
    ("single-source_1400Hz_40deg_1.0s", 1400.0),
    ("single-source_4700Hz_120deg_1.0s", 4700.0),
];

fn read_golden(name: &str) -> (Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>) {
    let text = fs::read_to_string(Path::new(GOLDEN_DIR).join(name))
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("cannot read golden file {name}: {e}"));
    text.lines()
        .skip(1)
        .map(|line| {
            let (a, s) = line.split_once(',').unwrap();
            (a.parse::<f64>().unwrap(), s.parse::<f64>().unwrap())
        })
        .unzip()
}

fn argmax(v: &[f64]) -> usize {
    (0..v.len()).max_by(|&a, &b| v[a].total_cmp(&v[b])).unwrap()
}

/// Compare a musicrs spectrum against both golden variants of `prefix`.
fn check(prefix: &str, angles: &[f64], spectrum: &[f64]) {
    // Value-by-value against pyMUSIC with a Hermitian eigensolver
    let (g_angles, g_spectrum) = read_golden(&format!("{prefix}.eigh.csv"));
    assert_eq!(angles.len(), g_angles.len(), "{prefix}: grid size differs");
    for (a, g) in angles.iter().zip(&g_angles) {
        assert!(
            (a - g).abs() < 1e-9,
            "{prefix}: angle grid differs ({a} vs {g})"
        );
    }
    let err = spectrum
        .iter()
        .zip(&g_spectrum)
        .map(|(s, g)| (s - g).abs() / g.abs())
        .fold(0.0, f64::max);
    println!("{prefix}: max relative error vs eigh {err:.3e}");
    assert!(
        err < REL_TOLERANCE,
        "{prefix}: deviates from pyMUSIC (eigh) by {err:.3e}"
    );

    // Peak location against pyMUSIC as published (within one grid step, circularly)
    let (_, orig) = read_golden(&format!("{prefix}.eig.csv"));
    let (ours, theirs) = (argmax(spectrum), argmax(&orig));
    let n = spectrum.len();
    let steps = (ours + n - theirs) % n;
    let steps = steps.min(n - steps);
    println!(
        "{prefix}: peak {:.1}° vs pyMUSIC (eig) {:.1}°",
        angles[ours].to_degrees(),
        angles[theirs].to_degrees()
    );
    assert!(
        steps <= 1,
        "{prefix}: peak differs from pyMUSIC (eig) by {steps} grid steps"
    );
}

#[test]
fn narrowband_spectrum_matches_pymusic() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    for (stem, freq) in CASES {
        let (_, data) =
            common::read_wav_4ch(&Path::new(common::DATA_DIR).join(format!("{stem}.wav")));
        let analytic: Vec<Vec<_>> = (0..data.nrows())
            .map(|m| analytic_signal(&data.row(m).iter().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>()))

        let x = DMatrix::from_fn(data.nrows(), data.ncols(), |m, t| analytic[m][t]);

        let noise = est.noise_subspace(&cov, 1);

//
// These tests mirror the structure of `integration_test.rs` but exercise
// IFB-MUSIC rather than narrowband MUSIC.  The composite source at each angle
// is formed by superimposing *all* available single-frequency recordings at
// that DOA, making the signal genuinely broadband across the entire test
// frequency range (300 Hz – 9.1 kHz).

/// All nine available test frequencies (Hz), matching the WAV file corpus.
const ALL_FREQS: [u32; 9] = [300, 1400, 2500, 3600, 4700, 5800, 6900, 8000, 9100];

/// All five ground-truth DOA angles (degrees) in the test corpus.
const ALL_ANGLES_DEG: [u32; 5] = [0, 40, 80, 120, 160];

/// IFB-MUSIC correctly estimates the DOA of a nine-tone broadband single source
/// at every available ground-truth angle.
///
/// For each angle in {0°, 40°, 80°, 120°, 160°} the nine single-frequency
/// recordings at that angle (300 – 9100 Hz) are summed to form a composite
/// signal.  IFB-MUSIC is run with targeted STFT bins at each component
/// frequency.  The estimated DOA must be within ±5° of the true angle
/// (accounting for the linear-array mirror ambiguity).
///
/// All failures are collected and reported together at the end.
#[test]
fn test_broadband_single_source_doa_nine_tone() {
    let estimator = MusicEstimator::default();
    let tolerance_deg = TOL_TARGETED;

    let bins: Vec<usize> = ALL_FREQS
        .iter()
        .map(|&f| freq_to_bin(f as f64, NFFT, SAMPLE_RATE))
        .collect();

    let mut failures: Vec<String> = Vec::new();

    for &doa_deg in &ALL_ANGLES_DEG {
        let data = load_composite_source_n(doa_deg, &ALL_FREQS, "2.0s");

        let (spectrum, angles) = estimator.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&bins));
        let estimated_deg = find_peak_doa_deg(&spectrum, &angles);
        let err = min_equivalent_error_deg(estimated_deg, doa_deg as f64);

        if err > tolerance_deg {
            failures.push(format!(
                "DOA {}°: expected {:.1}° (or {:.1}°), got {:.1}° (error {:.1}°)",
                doa_deg,
                doa_deg as f64,
                360.0 - doa_deg as f64,
                estimated_deg,
                err
            ));
        }
    }

    if !failures.is_empty() {
        panic!(
            "{}/{} angles failed nine-tone IFB-MUSIC test (tolerance ±{:.0}°):\n{}",
            failures.len(),
            ALL_ANGLES_DEG.len(),
            tolerance_deg,
            failures.join("\n")
        );
    }

    println!(
        "All {} nine-tone broadband DOA tests passed (tolerance ±{:.0}°).",
        ALL_ANGLES_DEG.len(),
        tolerance_deg
    );
}

/// IFB-MUSIC correctly estimates the DOA of composite broadband sources formed
/// from every distinct low / mid / high frequency triple available in the test
/// corpus, across all five ground-truth angles.
///
/// The frequencies are divided into three sub-Nyquist spectral bands (all ≤ 8 kHz;
/// 9100 Hz is excluded because it lies above the 8 kHz Nyquist and its energy
/// appears at the aliased bin 6900 Hz in the single-sided STFT, making the
/// steering-vector frequency ambiguous — that case is covered by the narrowband
/// `test_single_source_doa` test which uses the correct sign-flip convention):
///  - Low : 300, 1400, 2500 Hz
///  - Mid : 3600, 4700, 5800 Hz
///  - High: 6900, 8000 Hz
///
/// Tested triples are all 18 combinations (one frequency from each band), giving
/// 18 × 5 = 90 (angle, triple) pairs.  IFB-MUSIC is run with three targeted
/// STFT bins — one per component.  Tolerance: ±5°.
///
/// All failures are collected and reported together at the end.
#[test]
#[ignore = "slow"]
fn test_broadband_single_source_doa_frequency_triples() {
    let estimator = MusicEstimator::default();
    let tolerance_deg = TOL_TARGETED;

    let low_band: [u32; 3] = [300, 1400, 2500];
    let mid_band: [u32; 3] = [3600, 4700, 5800];
    // 9100 Hz is above the 8 kHz Nyquist; limit high band to sub-Nyquist only.
    let high_band: [u32; 2] = [6900, 8000];

    let mut failures: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut total = 0usize;

    for &fl in &low_band {
        for &fm in &mid_band {
            for &fh in &high_band {
                let triple = [fl, fm, fh];
                let bins: Vec<usize> = triple
                    .iter()
                    .map(|&f| freq_to_bin(f as f64, NFFT, SAMPLE_RATE))
                    .collect();

                for &doa_deg in &ALL_ANGLES_DEG {
                    let data = load_composite_source(doa_deg, &triple, "2.0s");

                    let (spectrum, angles) =
                        estimator.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&bins));
                    let estimated_deg = find_peak_doa_deg(&spectrum, &angles);
                    let err = min_equivalent_error_deg(estimated_deg, doa_deg as f64);

                    if err > tolerance_deg {
                        failures.push(format!(
                            "DOA {doa_deg}°, triple {fl}+{fm}+{fh} Hz (bins {bins:?}): got {estimated_deg:.1}° (error {err:.1}°)"
                        ));
                    }
                    total += 1;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if !failures.is_empty() {
        panic!(
            "{}/{} (angle, triple) pairs failed IFB-MUSIC frequency-triple test \
             (tolerance ±{:.0}°):\n{}",
            failures.len(),
            total,
            tolerance_deg,
            failures.join("\n")
        );
    }

    println!(
        "All {total} (angle, triple) broadband DOA tests passed (tolerance ±{tolerance_deg:.0}°)."
    );
}

/// Add additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) to a multichannel signal.
///
/// The noise level is specified as a signal-to-noise ratio in decibels:
/// ```text
/// SNR_dB = 10 · log10(P_signal / P_noise)
/// ```
/// The signal power is computed per-channel and averaged across channels so
/// that the SNR is consistent regardless of the signal amplitude.
///
/// `seed` makes the noise reproducible across test runs.
fn add_white_noise(signal: &DMatrix<f64>, snr_db: f64, seed: u64) -> DMatrix<f64> {
    let n_channels = signal.nrows();
    let n_samples = signal.ncols();

    // Mean signal power across all channels and samples
    let signal_power: f64 =
        signal.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f64>() / (n_channels * n_samples) as f64;

    // Desired noise standard deviation derived from the target SNR
    let noise_std = (signal_power / 10.0_f64.powf(snr_db / 10.0)).sqrt();

    let mut rng = Lcg::new(seed);
    let mut noisy = signal.clone();
    for sample in noisy.iter_mut() {
        *sample += noise_std * rng.next_gaussian();
    }
    noisy
}

/// Read a 4-channel, 24-bit PCM WAV file with `hound` and return
/// `(sample_rate, data)` where `data` is a `(4 × n_samples)` real matrix
/// normalised to `[-1, 1]`.
fn read_wav_4ch(path: &PathBuf) -> (u32, DMatrix<f64>) {
    let mut reader = hound::WavReader::open(path).expect("Failed to open WAV file");
    let spec = reader.spec();
    assert_eq!(spec.channels, 4, "Expected 4-channel WAV");
    assert_eq!(spec.bits_per_sample, 24, "Expected 24-bit PCM");

    let raw_samples: Vec<i32> = reader
        .samples::<i32>()
        .map(|s| s.expect("Sample read error"))
        .collect();

    let n_channels = spec.channels as usize;
    let n_samples = raw_samples.len() / n_channels;
    let scale = 2.0_f64.powi(23);

    let mut data = DMatrix::<f64>::zeros(n_channels, n_samples);
    for (idx, &sample) in raw_samples.iter().enumerate() {
        let ch = idx % n_channels;
        let t = idx / n_channels;
        data[(ch, t)] = sample as f64 / scale;
    }

    (spec.sample_rate, data)
}

/// Parse metadata from a test-data filename.
/// Format: `single-source_<freq>Hz_<doa>deg_<duration>s.wav`
fn parse_test_file_meta_params(path: &Path) -> Option<Vec<String>> {
    path.file_name()
        .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
        .map(|file_name| {
            file_name
                .strip_suffix(".wav")
                .unwrap()
                .split('_')
                .map(str::to_owned)
                .collect()
        })
}

/// Core helper shared by all SNR-level tests.
///
/// Loads every WAV from `tests/data/single-source/`, corrupts it with AWGN at
/// `snr_db`, runs the MUSIC estimator, and asserts that the error is within
/// `tolerance_deg` for each file.
fn run_noisy_doa_test(snr_db: f64, tolerance_deg: f64) {
    let estimator = MusicEstimator::default();

    let paths = fs::read_dir("./tests/data/single-source")
        .expect("Test data directory not found")
        .filter(|p| {
            let p = p.as_ref().unwrap().path();
            p.extension().and_then(|ext| ext.to_str()) == Some("wav")
        });

    let mut total = 0usize;
    let mut failures: Vec<String> = Vec::new();

    for (file_idx, entry) in paths.enumerate() {
        let path = entry.unwrap().path();
        let parts = parse_test_file_meta_params(&path).unwrap();

        let freq_hz: f64 = parts[1].strip_suffix("Hz").unwrap().parse().unwrap();
        let true_doa_deg: f64 = parts[2].strip_suffix("deg").unwrap().parse().unwrap();

        // ── Read WAV, add noise, build complex signal matrix ──────────────────
        let (sample_rate, real_data) = read_wav_4ch(&path);
        // Use file index as part of the seed so each file gets different noise
        // while remaining reproducible across test runs.
        let seed = (snr_db as u64).wrapping_mul(1_000) ^ (file_idx as u64).wrapping_mul(7_919);
        let noisy_data = add_white_noise(&real_data, snr_db, seed);

        let n_mics = noisy_data.nrows();
        let n_samples = noisy_data.ncols();

        let mut complex_data = DMatrix::<num_complex::Complex<f64>>::zeros(n_mics, n_samples);
        for m in 0..n_mics {
            let row: Vec<f64> = noisy_data.row(m).iter().copied().collect();
            let analytic = analytic_signal(&row);
            for (t, c) in analytic.into_iter().enumerate() {
                complex_data[(m, t)] = c;
            }
        }

        // ── Estimate DOA ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        let estimated_angles = estimator.estimate_doa(&complex_data, 1, freq_hz);

        let estimated_deg = if estimated_angles.is_empty() {
            failures.push(format!(
                "{:?}: no peak found (expected {:.1}°, SNR {snr_db:.0} dB)",
                path.file_name().unwrap(),
                true_doa_deg
            ));
            total += 1;
            continue;
        } else {
            estimated_angles[0].to_degrees()
        };

        // ── Check accuracy ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        let nyquist = sample_rate as f64 / 2.0;
        let is_nyquist = (freq_hz - nyquist).abs() < 0.5;
        let angular_dist = |a: f64, b: f64| -> f64 {
            let d = (a - b).abs();
            if d > 180.0 { 360.0 - d } else { d }
        };
        let equivalent_angles: &[f64] = if is_nyquist {
            &[
                true_doa_deg,
                360.0 - true_doa_deg,
                180.0 - true_doa_deg,
                180.0 + true_doa_deg,
            ]
        } else {
            &[true_doa_deg, 360.0 - true_doa_deg]
        };
        let diff_wrapped = equivalent_angles
            .iter()
            .map(|&t| angular_dist(estimated_deg, t))
            .fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min);

        if diff_wrapped > tolerance_deg {
            failures.push(format!(
                "{} @ SNR {snr_db:.0} dB: expected {:.1}° (equivalents: {:?}), \
                 got {:.1}° (error {:.1}°)",
                path.file_name().unwrap().to_str().unwrap(),
                true_doa_deg,
                equivalent_angles,
                estimated_deg,
                diff_wrapped,
            ));
        }
        total += 1;
    }

    if !failures.is_empty() {
        panic!(
            "{}/{} files failed noisy DOA test (SNR {snr_db:.0} dB, tolerance ±{tolerance_deg:.0}°):\n{}",
            failures.len(),
            total,
            failures.join("\n")
        );
    }

    println!(
        "All {total} noisy DOA tests passed \
         (SNR {snr_db:.0} dB, tolerance ±{tolerance_deg:.0}°)."
    );
}

//! Broadband single-source integration tests for IFB-MUSIC.
//!
//! Each test constructs a **composite-tone source** by superimposing three
//! single-frequency recordings from `tests/data/single-source/` that share
//! the same true DOA.  The resulting signal mimics a broadband source emitting
//! three simultaneous sinusoidal tones at a known direction.
//!
//! IFB-MUSIC (`ifb_music_spectrum`) is then run on the real-valued composite
//! data and the estimated DOA is checked against the ground-truth angle.
//!
//! Tolerance: ±10° (relaxed slightly versus the narrowband ±5° because the
//! geometric-mean combination spans bins that may carry little signal energy
//! when `bins = None`; targeted-bin tests use the tighter ±5° tolerance).

use std::path::PathBuf;

use musicrs::MusicEstimator;
use nalgebra::DMatrix;

// ─── Constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const SAMPLE_RATE: f64 = 16_000.0;
const N_MICS: usize = 4;

/// Default NFFT for IFB-MUSIC.  At 16 kHz this gives a bin width of
/// 16000 / 1024 ≈ 15.6 Hz, well below the lowest component tone (300 Hz).
const NFFT: usize = 1024;

/// Tolerance for all-bin IFB-MUSIC tests (degrees).
const TOL_ALL_BINS: f64 = 10.0;

/// Tolerance for targeted-bin IFB-MUSIC tests (degrees).
const TOL_TARGETED: f64 = 5.0;

// ─── Helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn wav_path(freq_hz: u32, doa_deg: u32, duration_s: &str) -> PathBuf {
    PathBuf::from(format!(
        "./tests/data/single-source/single-source_{freq_hz}Hz_{doa_deg}deg_{duration_s}.wav"
    ))
}

/// Read a 4-channel, 24-bit PCM WAV file and return a `(4 × n_samples)` matrix
/// with amplitudes normalised to `[−1, 1]`.
fn read_wav_4ch(path: &PathBuf) -> DMatrix<f64> {
    let mut reader =
        hound::WavReader::open(path).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("Failed to open {path:?}: {e}"));
    let spec = reader.spec();
    assert_eq!(spec.channels, 4, "Expected 4-channel WAV");
    assert_eq!(spec.bits_per_sample, 24, "Expected 24-bit PCM");

    let raw: Vec<i32> = reader
        .samples::<i32>()
        .map(|s| s.expect("Sample read error"))
        .collect();
    let n_samples = raw.len() / N_MICS;
    let scale = 2.0_f64.powi(23);

    let mut data = DMatrix::<f64>::zeros(N_MICS, n_samples);
    for (idx, &s) in raw.iter().enumerate() {
        let ch = idx % N_MICS;
        let t = idx / N_MICS;
        data[(ch, t)] = s as f64 / scale;
    }
    data
}

/// Load three single-frequency WAV files at the same `doa_deg` and sum them
/// channel-by-channel, producing a composite broadband recording.
///
/// All files are trimmed to the shortest available recording length before
/// superimposition so that the matrix dimensions are consistent.
fn load_composite_source(doa_deg: u32, freqs_hz: &[u32; 3], duration_s: &str) -> DMatrix<f64> {
    load_composite_source_n(doa_deg, freqs_hz, duration_s)
}

/// Load an arbitrary number of single-frequency WAV files at the same `doa_deg`
/// and sum them channel-by-channel.  All recordings are trimmed to the shortest
/// length before superimposition.
fn load_composite_source_n(doa_deg: u32, freqs_hz: &[u32], duration_s: &str) -> DMatrix<f64> {
    assert!(!freqs_hz.is_empty(), "need at least one frequency");
    let signals: Vec<DMatrix<f64>> = freqs_hz
        .iter()
        .map(|&f| read_wav_4ch(&wav_path(f, doa_deg, duration_s)))
        .collect();

    let n_samples = signals.iter().map(|s| s.ncols()).min().unwrap();
    let mut composite = DMatrix::<f64>::zeros(N_MICS, n_samples);
    for sig in &signals {
        composite += sig.columns(0, n_samples);
    }

    let mut peaks: Vec<(f64, f64)> = (0..len)
        .filter_map(|i| {

fn freq_to_bin(freq_hz: f64, nfft: usize, sample_rate: f64) -> usize {

I read `src/` and all six test files. Below are the gaps, most important first. Several of them hide what look like real bugs.

## 1. Code paths no test reaches

- **More than one source.** Every test uses `n_sources = 1`, but separating several sources is what MUSIC is for. Nothing tests two sources at different angles, whether `find_peaks` returns them in the right order, or `ifb_music_spectrum` with `n_sources > 1`.
- **Any array other than the Kinect line.** All mics have `y = 0`, so the `p[1] * dir[1]` term in `steering_vector` is always zero, and every test has to accept θ or 360° − θ. A 2-D array (a triangle or square) would test that the y term is right and that the estimator can tell θ from 360° − θ.
- **Search ranges other than the full circle.** Only `(0, 2π)` is used. `find_peaks` (`src/music.rs`) wraps around with `% len`, which only makes sense on a full circle. With `(0, π)`, the first and last angles are treated as neighbours, so it can report a peak that isn't there or miss one at the edge. A test with a source near 0° or 180° on a half-circle range should expose this.
- **The Nyquist and above-Nyquist branches of `steering_vector`.** Nothing checks the sign flip above Nyquist, the real-valued vector at Nyquist, or the 0.5 Hz tolerance. Only the slow, ignored integration test reaches them, and only indirectly. Nothing checks the `+j2πfτ` sign convention directly either.

## 2. Weak unit tests

- **`hermitian_eigen`:** both eigenvalue tests sort the result again before asserting. So the function's promise to return eigenvalues in ascending order is never tested, and that order is exactly what `noise_subspace` relies on. No test checks `A·v = λ·v`.
- **`noise_subspace`:** the tests only feed it the identity matrix, where every orthonormal basis passes. Nothing checks that it actually keeps the eigenvectors with the smallest eigenvalues.
- **`estimate_doa_synthetic_source`:** it builds its data with `est.steering_vector` itself, so it only shows the code agrees with itself. The doctest on `estimate_doa_from_real` is the only one that models the physics independently.
- **`find_peaks`:** the test only checks the first returned value, `peaks[0]`, not the second. Nothing covers a flat or plateau spectrum (no peaks, so `estimate_doa` returns an empty vector), `n = 0`, or a peak at index 0 or the last index.
- **`spectrum`:** when the denominator is zero the code returns `f64::INFINITY`; no test reaches that.

## 3. Edge cases and panics

- `analytic_signal(&[])` will panic: `spectrum[0] *= 1.0` indexes into an empty vector. Odd lengths and length 1 are also untested, and odd N handles the Nyquist bin differently. Nothing checks the basic property `Re(z) == x`.
- No `#[should_panic]` tests for the documented panics: `n_sources >= n_antennas`, a row-count mismatch in `estimate_doa_from_real`, and `stft` with `nfft = 0` or `no_overlap >= nfft`.
- **`stft`:** tests check only the output shape and which bin is largest, never actual DFT values. They never check what overlapping windows contain or input shorter than `nfft`. In that last case `ifb_music_spectrum` takes its `n_windows == 0` early return, which is also untested. CLAUDE.md says the STFT has a "configurable window", but `stft()` has no window parameter. Either the docs or the code is wrong.
- **`ifb_music_spectrum`:** nothing tests that bins `>= nfft/2+1` are silently skipped. Nothing checks the geometric mean directly (for example, passing the same bin twice should give the same spectrum as passing it once).
- **Possible overflow in `ifb_music_spectrum`:** with `bins = None` it multiplies all the per-bin spectra before taking the root (512 of them at `nfft = 1024`). That product could overflow to infinity or underflow to zero. `ifb_music_spectrum_values_finite_positive` only uses 3 targeted bins. I haven't confirmed this; a finiteness test with `bins = None` would settle it. Computing the mean of the logarithms instead of the product would avoid the risk.
- **Too few samples:** nothing tests `n_samples < n_antennas`, where the covariance matrix is rank-deficient.

## 4. Gaps in the data-driven tests

- **Noise:** only narrowband is tested with noise. IFB/broadband has no noise test, and nothing tests two noisy sources. The noisy tests also rebuild the analytic-signal step by hand and call `estimate_doa` instead of `estimate_doa_from_real`.
- **Golden tests:** only 3 cases, all 1.0 s, all below 4.7 kHz. There's no IFB golden with several bins, and nothing pins the intended difference from pyMUSIC at or above Nyquist (a test that fixes musicrs's own output there would catch accidental changes).
- **Tolerances:** the angle grid steps by 0.5°, but every test accepts ±5° (±20° at 1 dB SNR), so a 4° regression would pass. Logging the worst error and tightening the limit to just above it would catch drift.
- **Composite tests:** `test_broadband_single_source_doa_nine_tone` includes 9100 Hz. `freq_to_bin` aliases that to the 6900 Hz bin, so that bin is counted twice in the geometric mean, which the test doesn't seem to intend.

## 5. Test code upkeep

`noisy_data_test.rs` and `broadband_test.rs` each have their own copy of `read_wav_4ch`, filename parsing and angle-error helpers instead of using `tests/common/mod.rs`. `noisy_data_test.rs` also doesn't sort the file list, so its noise seeds depend on directory order.

There's no coverage tool installed (`cargo llvm-cov` isn't available), so this list comes from reading the code. Adding `cargo-llvm-cov` would confirm it.

**My suggestion for what to write first:** a two-source synthetic test, a 2-D array test, a half-circle search-range test (likely exposing the `find_peaks` bug), an ascending-order check for `hermitian_eigen`, unit tests for the two Nyquist branches, and the empty-input `analytic_signal` case. They're all small and fast, so they wouldn't need `#[ignore = "slow"]`. I can do them on a `feat/test-gaps` branch.

content.text:
I fixed the `find_peaks` bug and committed it as `000068f` on a new branch, `fix/find-peaks-search-interval`. It isn't pushed yet.

**The bug:** `find_peaks` always treated the first and last grid angles as neighbours, even when the search range wasn't the full circle. On a `[0, π)` range, an edge point was compared with the value at the opposite end, so a real peak at one end disappeared whenever the other end was higher.

**Reproducing it:** I first wrote `estimate_doa_finds_sources_at_both_ends_of_half_circle`, which puts two sources on the first and last grid angles of `[0, π)`. On the old code it failed: it asked for 2 peaks and got only one, `[0.0]`.

**The fix** (`src/music.rs`):
- `find_peaks` now takes a `circular` flag. Ends wrap around only when it's set. Otherwise each end is compared with its one neighbour, so a source at the edge of the range (say 0° with `[0, π)`) is still found.
- A new private `covers_full_circle()` sets the flag when `search_interval` spans exactly 2π. `estimate_doa` uses it.
- I documented on `search_interval` that the grid includes the start, excludes the end, and wraps only for a full 2π span.

**New tests:** besides the reproduction above, there are unit tests for wrap-around on a full circle, for both ends counting as peaks on an open range, and for `covers_full_circle` (`(0, 2π)` and `(-π, π)` wrap; `(0, π)` and `(0, 1.9π)` don't). All are fast.

`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -- --include-ignored` all pass. Nothing changes for the default full-circle range: the WAV, golden and broadband tests give the same results as before.

**Still open:** if `search_interval` spans more than 2π, the grid repeats angles. That's still treated as an open range, which you probably never want; rejecting it outright would also be reasonable.

Next is the rest of the list: two-source and 2-D array tests, an ascending-order check for `hermitian_eigen`, unit tests for the Nyquist branches, and empty input to `analytic_signal`. Should I open a PR for this fix first, or continue on a separate `feat/test-gaps` branch and open both together?

I opened the `find_peaks` PR, [#8](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/pull/8), and added the planned tests on `feat/test-gaps`. The new tests found two more real bugs, which I fixed there too. That's 6 commits; none of them pushed yet.

**Two more bugs, both fixed:**
- **`analytic_signal` on empty or odd-length input** (`cf37423`): empty input panicked. For odd lengths the output's real part didn't equal the input, because the code treated bin `n/2` as a Nyquist bin, which only exists for even lengths. It now works like `scipy.signal.hilbert`. The WAV recordings all have even length, so their results don't change.
- **Overflow in `ifb_music_spectrum`** (`310d7a0`): with `bins = None` and `nfft = 1024`, multiplying 512 per-bin spectra overflowed. On `single-source_300Hz_80deg_1.0s`, 26 of 720 values came out as `inf`, and the highest value landed on one of them. It now averages logarithms instead, which gives the same geometric mean without overflowing.

**New tests (all fast, none marked slow):**
- **`b04ae9a`:** eigenvalues must come back in ascending order (the old tests re-sorted them first), and `A·v = λ·v` must hold. The noise subspace must be orthogonal to the sources, and too many sources must panic.
- **`d79ab51`:** the steering vector's `+j2πfτ` sign below Nyquist, the conjugated vector above Nyquist, and the real vector within 0.5 Hz of Nyquist.
- **`a4f718a`:** a new `tests/synthetic_test.rs` with a square and a five-mic array: one source anywhere on the circle with no mirror image, two sources, and three sources. The signals are built from the array geometry, not from `steering_vector`. When I temporarily flipped the steering sign, all three DOA tests failed; the existing Kinect tests probably wouldn't notice that. CLAUDE.md now lists this file.
- **`310d7a0`:** an IFB spectrum with all bins must be finite. A bin repeated three times must equal the single bin, out-of-range bins must be skipped, and data shorter than one window gives a flat spectrum.
- **`dea520f`:** the two `stft` argument panics, and overlapping windows starting at the right sample.

`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -- --include-ignored` all pass.

- **Branch naming:** CLAUDE.md asks for bug fixes on `fix/` branches, but these two are mixed in with tests on a `feat/` branch. I can split them into their own `fix/` branches if you prefer.

- **Broadband results:** with `bins = None`, the IFB peak is far off for a single tone (281° for a 40° source in my check), because bins without signal drown it out. That's how the method behaves, not a crash, so I didn't add a test for it.

- **`analytic_signal` on empty or odd-length input**: empty input panicked on `spectrum[0]`. For odd N, bin N/2 was treated as a Nyquist bin and left undoubled, so `Re(z)` no longer equalled the input. Now matches `scipy.signal.hilbert`; even-length input (all WAV fixtures) is unchanged.
- **`ifb_music_spectrum` overflow**: the per-bin spectra were multiplied before taking the root. With `bins = None` at `nfft = 1024`, the product of 512 spectra overflowed to `inf` on `single-source_300Hz_80deg_1.0s` (26 of 720 angles) and the argmax landed on one of them. The geometric mean is now a mean of logarithms.

### New tests (all fast)
- `hermitian_eigen` returns ascending eigenvalues (the old tests re-sorted before asserting) and satisfies `A·v = λ·v`; the noise subspace is orthogonal to the sources; too many sources panic.
- `steering_vector`: `+j2πfτ` convention below Nyquist, conjugate above, real within 0.5 Hz of Nyquist.
- `tests/synthetic_test.rs`: square and pentagon arrays with 1, 2 and 3 sources, built from the geometry rather than `steering_vector`. Flipping the steering sign makes all three DOA tests fail.
- IFB: finite with all bins, repeated bin equals single bin, out-of-range bins skipped, data shorter than a window is flat.
- `stft`: argument panics and overlapping-window start positions.

<result>def IFBMUSICSpectrum(data, micPositions, nfft, amountOfSources=1, angleStepsNum=720,\
                     searchInterval=(0, 2 * np.pi), samplingRate=16000, bins=None):
    """
    Returns an IFB MUSIC spectrum. The narrowband spectrums are merged by geometric mean.

    @param data sampled data (real part of the signal)
    @param nfft window size of for the STFT in samples
    @param amountOfSources assumed number of sources
    @param angleStepsNum amount of angle to analyze
    @param searchInterval tuple with the first element as starting angle and the second element is end angle
    @param rate the data are sampled
    @param bins array or range determining the frequency bins to use
    @return IFB MUSIC spectrum
    """

    narrowBandEst = MUSICEst(antennaPositions=micPositions, angleStepsNum=angleStepsNum,\
                             searchInterval=searchInterval)

    # STFT for all microphones (format: [microphone, frequency bins, time])
    stft = np.empty((data.shape[0], nfft // 2 + 1, data.shape[1] // nfft), dtype=np.complex)
    for i in range(data.shape[0]):
        stft[i, :, :] = STFT(np.asarray(data)[i, :], nfft)

    # Physical frequencies for the MUSIC algorithm
    freqs = rfftfreq(nfft, 1 / samplingRate)

    mergedSpectrums = np.ones(angleStepsNum)
    if bins == None:
        bins = range(nfft // 2 + 1)

    # Calculate narrowband spectrums and merging them with geometric mean
    for binIdx in bins:
        crossSpectrum = np.matrix(np.zeros((stft.shape[0], stft.shape[0]), dtype=np.complex))
        for j in range(stft.shape[2]):
            curDFT = np.matrix(stft[:, binIdx, j]).transpose()
            crossSpectrum += curDFT * curDFT.transpose().conjugate()
        crossSpectrum /= stft.shape[2]
        noiseMat = narrowBandEst.getNoiseMat(crossSpectrum, amountOfSources)
        spectrum, angleBins = narrowBandEst.getSpectrum(noiseMat, freqs[binIdx], noiseMatMode='spec')
        mergedSpectrums *= spectrum

    mergedSpectrums = mergedSpectrums ** (1 / len(bins))

    return mergedSpectrums, angleBins

content.text:
I opened [PR #9](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/pull/9) from `feat/test-gaps` and pushed the remaining items onto it. It now has 8 commits, and I updated the PR description to match. `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -- --include-ignored` all pass.

**The broadband results:** when every bin is used, the method itself gives poor results; it isn't a bug. IFB-MUSIC computes one MUSIC spectrum per frequency bin and averages them, with every bin counting equally. A single tone fills maybe 1–3 of the 512 bins at `nfft = 1024`. The other bins hold only noise and leakage, but MUSIC still treats their strongest direction as "the source". So hundreds of spectra pointing in arbitrary directions outvote a few correct ones, which is how a 40° source ended up at 281°. The usual remedies are to keep only bins with real energy (for example, a total power well above the median) or to weight each bin by its power. I can add either as an option to `ifb_music_spectrum`.

**What changed since the PR opened:**
- **Shared helpers:** the noisy and broadband tests now use `tests/common` instead of their own copies of the WAV reader and angle helpers. A new `ErrorLog` lists every failing case and prints the worst error per test, so tolerances can be checked with `cargo test -- --nocapture`. The noisy test now reads files in sorted order, so its random noise no longer depends on directory order.
- **Tighter tolerances:** every clean recording lands exactly on its true angle, so the old ±5° limit could hide a 4° regression. New limits, with the measured worst errors:

| Test | Worst error | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clean recordings (narrowband, IFB, broadband) | 0.00° | ±5–10° | ±0.5° (one grid step) |
| Broadband frequency triples | 2.5° | ±5° | ±3° |
| Noise at 10 / 5 / 1 dB SNR | 3.0 / 1.5 / 5.0° | ±10 / 15 / 20° | ±5 / 5 / 8° |

  The noisy limits keep some headroom because their worst case depends on the random noise: at 10 dB it came out worse than at 5 dB. CLAUDE.md now describes these tolerances.
- **9100 Hz bin:** the nine-tone test no longer counts the 6900 Hz bin twice (9100 Hz aliases onto it).
- **More golden cases:** I generated these with the original pyMUSIC using `tests/golden/generate_golden.py`. They cover a 2 s recording at 0° (endfire), one at 160°, 6.9 kHz, and a three-tone composite using three IFB bins. All match pyMUSIC (with its Hermitian solver `eigh`) to within 4e-6 relative error. The existing golden files came out byte-for-byte identical.
- **Golden peak check:** the comparison with pyMUSIC as published now accepts the mirror-image angle. On the composite, pyMUSIC's peak was at 320° and ours at 40°. The two peaks are equally high on the line array, so which one wins comes down to rounding.

I didn't add golden cases at or above Nyquist (8 kHz). musicrs deliberately handles those differently from pyMUSIC, so the values would differ.

Should I add energy-based bin selection for broadband next? Note that PR #8 and PR #9 both edit `src/music.rs`, so whichever merges second may need a small rebase.
